title: Capacity and Volume: Millilitres and Litres
seo_title: Grade 5 Capacity and Volume Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Estimate, measure, record, compare and order capacity and volume using measuring instruments such as measuring spoons, measuring cups and measuring jugs; use millilitres (mℓ) and litres (ℓ); calculate and solve problems involving capacity and volume; convert between litres and millilitres.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 5 capacity and volume worksheets: millilitres and litres, reading measuring jugs, converting units and problems. 100 questions with memos.
key_sub: Read what each mark on the jug is worth.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Capacity is how much a container can hold. Volume is how much space something takes up.
  • We measure liquids in millilitres (mℓ) and litres (ℓ). 1 ℓ = 1 000 mℓ.
  • Use mℓ for a teaspoon or a cup, and ℓ for a bucket or a bath.
  • On a measuring jug, find what each mark is worth before you read it.

Examples

Example

A 2 ℓ bottle fills 250 mℓ glasses

2 ℓ = 2 000 mℓ

2 000 ÷ 250

Answer: 8 glasses

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
100 mℓ in a litre1 ℓ = 1 000 mℓ.
The wrong intervalWork out each mark first.
Different unitsChange to mℓ first.

items.q: A jug has a line every 250 mℓ. How many spaces are there from 0 up to 1 ℓ?
items.e: 1 ℓ = 1 000 mℓ. Count by 250: 250, 500, 750, 1 000. That is 4 spaces. Do not count the 0 line as a space.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 mℓ. There are 4 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 200 mℓ ÷ 4 = 50 mℓ. Count the spaces after 200 mℓ: 250 mℓ, 300 mℓ, 350 mℓ. So it is 350 mℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 mℓ. There are 4 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 200 mℓ ÷ 4 = 50 mℓ. Count the spaces after 600 mℓ: 650 mℓ. So it is 650 mℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 250 mℓ. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 250 mℓ ÷ 5 = 50 mℓ. Count the spaces after 250 mℓ: 300 mℓ, 350 mℓ, 400 mℓ. So it is 400 mℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 250 mℓ. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 250 mℓ ÷ 5 = 50 mℓ. Count the spaces after 750 mℓ: 800 mℓ, 850 mℓ. So it is 850 mℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 100 mℓ. There are 4 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 100 mℓ ÷ 4 = 25 mℓ. Count the spaces after 100 mℓ: 125 mℓ, 150 mℓ, 175 mℓ. So it is 175 mℓ.

items.q: The water is halfway between two lines. How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 mℓ with 2 spaces, so each line is 100 mℓ. The water is halfway between 500 mℓ and 600 mℓ. Halfway is 550 mℓ.

items.q: The water is halfway between two lines. How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 mℓ with 2 spaces, so each line is 100 mℓ. The water is halfway between 200 mℓ and 300 mℓ. Halfway is 250 mℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: Each litre is split into 4 spaces, so each line is 1 000 ÷ 4 = 250 mℓ. The water is 1 line above 1 ℓ: 1 × 250 = 250 mℓ. So it is 1 ℓ 250 mℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: Each litre is split into 4 spaces, so each line is 1 000 ÷ 4 = 250 mℓ. The water is 3 lines above 1 ℓ: 3 × 250 = 750 mℓ. So it is 1 ℓ 750 mℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: Each litre is split into 10 spaces, so each line is 1 000 ÷ 10 = 100 mℓ. The water is 4 lines above 1 ℓ: 4 × 100 = 400 mℓ. So it is 1 ℓ 400 mℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: Each litre is split into 4 spaces, so each line is 1 000 ÷ 4 = 250 mℓ. The water is 3 lines above 2 ℓ: 3 × 250 = 750 mℓ. So it is 2 ℓ 750 mℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: Each litre is split into 5 spaces, so each line is 1 000 ÷ 5 = 200 mℓ. The water is 3 lines up from the bottom: 3 × 200 = 600 mℓ. It has not reached 1 ℓ.

items.q: How much more water is needed to fill the jug to 2 ℓ?
items.e: Each line is 250 mℓ, so the water is at 1 ℓ 750 mℓ. One more line reaches 2 ℓ. So 250 mℓ more is needed.

items.q: Thabo pours in 150 mℓ more water. How much water will be in the jug?
items.e: Each line is 50 mℓ, so the water is at 350 mℓ now. Pouring in means add: 350 + 150 = 500 mℓ.

items.q: Which amount is the same as 1 500 mℓ?
A jug has lines every 250 mℓ. The water is halfway between the 500 mℓ line and the 1 ℓ line. How much water is in the jug?
items.e: From 500 mℓ to 1 000 mℓ is 500 mℓ. Half of 500 is 250. 500 + 250 = 750 mℓ.

items.q: A jug has a line every 100 mℓ. The water is 4 lines above 1 ℓ. How much water is in the jug?
items.e: Each line is 100 mℓ, not 1 mℓ. 4 × 100 = 400 mℓ. So it is 1 ℓ 400 mℓ.
